river_checks.evidence: OPW Suir CFRAM station sheet: mean annual flow 45.277 m3/s for 1940–2005. Model mean 33.142; same order but lower, different period/model.

Cork County Council technical report cites long-term mean 47.4 m3/s. Initial cell mean 0.250 rejected; northern adjacent river-pattern cell mean 30.818. Different period/model; no calibration claimed.

Council submission on EPA archive gives long average 27.5 m3/s. Model mean 18.484; geographical position and eastward river-cell pattern support selection. Source prints station 15055; do not substitute that for verified OPW 18056.

OPW station statistics reproduced in EPA submission give Curranure downstream mean 15.039 m3/s, 1975–2004. Initial mean 0.291 rejected; northern river-pattern cell mean 8.159. Downstream reference is only a plausibility comparison, not an exact town calibration.

Engineering report gives upstream Scarrawalsh median 13.9 m3/s and expected average runoff 19.7 m3/s. Town model mean 13.475. Upstream reference, different period and statistic; evidence supports river-scale plausibility only.

Clare County Council report lists Fergus Ennis monthly means for 1972–77 from 1.42 to 25.83 m3/s; their unweighted average is about 12.35. Initial mean 2.988 investigated; western river-pattern cell mean 13.066. Tidal influence and Claureen confluence are limitations.
ESB report on EPA archive gives long-term Shannon average approximately 93 m3/s. Initial cell mean 0.754 rejected; western river-pattern cell mean 76.151. Flow is influenced by lakes and regulation.

EPA inspector report confirms upper Shannon location and quotes receiving-water/effluent ratio about 691:1 at median flow with effluent 2875 m3/day. Derived reference median approx 22.99 m3/s (691*2875/86400); compare model median, not mean. OPW live gauge is stale, so not used as current truth.
